reason: This is a conceptual position paper: it proposes a graph-based multi-agent framework (agents, plugins, roles, oracle agents, supervisor agents, halting) and sketches how Auto-GPT, BabyAGI, Gorilla, courtroom and software-development scenarios could be modeled in it. There are no experiments, no benchmarks, no measurements, and no comparisons of any intervention against a baseline; all claims are stated as possibilities ('can possibly address', 'could potentially be mitigated'). Any rule drawn from it — e.g. 'add a stateless supervisor agent to detect loops' or 'gate sensitive file/code actions through a memory-less oracle agent' — would rest entirely on the authors' speculation with no evidence of effect size, cost, or failure modes, so even an 'inferred' basis would lack the supporting finding the schema requires. No responsible candidate heuristic can be proposed from this text.
